DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# OPENING: Jesus had no human biological father

**Position.** I defend the standard reading. Jesus was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost without a man's seed. Joseph was his legal and reputed father, not the one who begat him. By "biological father" I mean a man who begat the child by his seed. I do not rest on any verse that denies the term in so many words. I rest on the verses that state how the child was conceived.

## 1. The text states the source of the conception

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** The Greek is *en gastri echousa ek pneumatos hagiou*. *Gastēr* (G1064) means womb. *Ek* (G1537) means out of, marking source and origin. The source of the pregnancy is the Holy Spirit, and the verse puts it "before they came together."

**[L3]** Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The Greek is *to en autē gennēthen ek pneumatos hagiou*. *Gennaō* (G1080) here means to be begotten or conceived, and *ek* again names the source. The angel gives this as the reason Joseph should not fear. If Joseph or another man had begotten the child, the explanation would be false.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 both use *ek* for the origin of the child, and both name the Holy Ghost. The text gives the origin of the begetting, and it is not human seed. That shuts out a human begetter.

## 2. Matthew breaks his own begetting formula at the end of the genealogy

**[L1]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** Every earlier link uses *egennēsen* (G1080, aorist active), "he begat," with the father as subject. At the end the verb changes to the passive *egennēthē*, "was born." The relative pronoun is *hēs* (G3739), feminine singular, "of whom," and so it points to Mary alone. Joseph is called *ton andra Marias*, "the husband of Mary," and is not said to have begotten Jesus.

**[L3]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." The Greek is *hōs enomizeto*. *Nomizō* (G3543) means to reckon, suppose, or hold by custom. Luke tells us the sonship was reputed, not actual.

**[L4]** Matthew drops "begat" at the one place where Joseph and Jesus meet, and he makes the feminine "of whom" the origin. Luke says "as was supposed" for the same relation. These two lines stand independently, and together they show the son-of-Joseph relation was legal and reputed.

## 3. Mary was a virgin before and through the conception

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** *Ginōskō* (G1097), "I know," is used here of sexual knowledge. The present tense with *ou* describes her standing: she has had no relations with a man.

**[L3]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." *Dio kai* means "for which cause also." The angel's answer to the question "How?" is that God's power will act, not a man.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." Here *eginōsken* (G1097) is again sexual knowledge. Joseph did not know her until the birth, so he did not father the child.

**[L4]** Mary's question in Luke 1:34 and the angel's answer in Luke 1:35 both treat the conception as having no man in it. Matthew 1:25 says the same from Joseph's side.

## 4. The prophecy and the means: "virgin" and "body prepared"

**[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

**[L2]** The Hebrew is *ʿalmāh* (H5959), a young woman of marriageable age, with *hārāh*, "conceived." Matthew 1:23 renders it with the Greek *parthenos* (G3933), "virgin."

**[L3]** Genesis 24:43 uses *ʿalmāh* of Rebekah, and Genesis 24:16 describes the same Rebekah as "a virgin, neither had any man known her." The word is used of a woman who had known no man.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child." The Holy Ghost inspired Matthew to apply the sign to this birth.

**[L3]** Hebrews 10:5: "but a body hast thou prepared me." *Katartizō* (G2675) means to fit, equip, or prepare. The body is spoken of as God's preparation.

**[L4]** Isaiah's *ʿalmāh*, Matthew's *parthenos*, and the "body prepared" of Hebrews 10:5 all point the same way. The child's body came by God's working in a virgin, and Joseph did not beget it.

## 5. Anticipated objections

**[L1]** Luke 2:48: "Thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."

**[L3]** Luke 3:23 says "as was supposed." Luke 2:33 says "Joseph and his mother marvelled." Joseph was in the household and in common speech the father. John 6:42 shows the crowd's language: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" That records what the crowd said, and Luke 3:23 corrects it with "as was supposed."

**[L1]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman."

**[L2]** The Greek is *genomenon ek gynaikos*, "come to be out of a woman." The text names the woman as the source and names no man, in agreement with Matthew 1:16.

**[L1]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."

**[L3]** Mary's descent is carried through the Davidic line that Luke 3:23 gives, "the son of Heli." Matthew 1:16 says Jesus was born "of whom," meaning Mary. So the Davidic descent comes through the mother and does not require Joseph as the begetter.

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on

1. The Holy Ghost is the stated source of the conception. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:18, "found with child of the Holy Ghost," and [L1] Matthew 1:20, "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost"; [L2] *ek* (G1537, out of) and *gennēthen* (G1080, begotten or conceived) name the origin, so no human seed is the source.
2. Matthew's genealogy ends the begetting formula before Jesus, and Luke calls the sonship supposed. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:16, "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus"; [L2] feminine *hēs* (G3739, of whom) and passive *egennēthē* (G1080, was born) after the active *egennēsen* (he begat) of Matthew 1:2; [L3] Luke 3:23, "as was supposed," with *enomizeto* (G3543, was reckoned).
3. Mary and Joseph had no union before the birth. Footing: [L1] Luke 1:34, "seeing I know not a man"; [L2] *ginōskō* (G1097, to know sexually); [L3] Matthew 1:25, "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
4. The prophecy and the means of the body point to a conception by God in a virgin. Footing: [L1] Isaiah 7:14, "a virgin shall conceive"; [L2] *ʿalmāh* (H5959, young woman) and *parthenos* (G3933, virgin); [L3] Genesis 24:43 with Genesis 24:16, and Hebrews 10:5, "a body hast thou prepared me."
5. Jesus had no human biological father. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:20, "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost," with [L1] Luke 1:35, "that holy thing which shall be born of thee"; [L2] *ek* (G1537, out of) as source, and *ginōskō* (G1097, to know sexually); [L3] Matthew 1:25 and Luke 3:23. Links 1 to 4 carry this: the source is the Holy Ghost, Joseph is only the reputed father, and there was no union.

# CHALLENGE: the record names Joseph as father and requires the seed out of a man's loins

**Position.** I answer the defender's chain, aiming at the keystone (D5): "Jesus had no human biological father." The promise of the seed requires flesh out of a man's body. The text names one man as the child's father, Joseph, "of the house of David." None of the defender's five links quotes a verse that says the child came without a man. Each link joins a true verse to an inference the verse does not carry. I set my own chain first, then break D1 to D5 on the defender's own verses.

## MY DECLARED CHAIN

**C1. The promised seed comes out of a man's loins, according to the flesh.**
- [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels." The seed comes from David's own body.
- [L3] Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne." Peter applies that oath to Christ, by the flesh.
- [L2] *osphys* (loins) in Acts 2:30 is the word Hebrews 7:10 uses of begetting: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him." That is a father's loins.
- [L3] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." Hebrews 7:14: "it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."
- [L4] The oath names loins and bowels. Peter and Paul apply it to Christ "according to the flesh." So the seed is a flesh seed out of a Davidic man's body. This rests on [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12, [L2] *osphys*, and [L3] Acts 2:30, Romans 1:3 and Hebrews 7:10.

**C2. The tribe is evident by the father's house.**
- [L1] Hebrews 7:14: "it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."
- [L3] Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers." Numbers 1:2 says the same: "by the house of their fathers."
- [L3] Ezra 2:62 shows the reverse. Priests "called after the name" of a wife's house (Ezra 2:61) "sought their register... but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood."
- [L4] Israel declares pedigree by the father's house, and the register was struck for men reckoned by a wife's house. So "evident... out of Juda" is evident through a father of Judah. This rests on [L1] Hebrews 7:14 and [L3] Numbers 1:18 and Ezra 2:61-62.

**C3. The one father the text names is Joseph, of the house of David.**
- [L1] Luke 2:48 is Mary's own mouth: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
- [L3] The narrator says "the parents brought in the child Jesus" (Luke 2:27) and "his parents went to Jerusalem" (Luke 2:41).
- [L3] Joseph's house is David's: "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David" (Luke 1:27), and "he was of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4).
- [L3] The angel calls him "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20).
- [L2] In Luke 2:48 the word is *ho patēr sou*, "thy father." In Luke 2:27 and 2:41 it is *goneis*, "parents," which is the begetters.
- [L4] Mary, who received the angel's word, calls Joseph "thy father." The narrator calls them "his parents." The Davidic house in the record is Joseph's. This rests on [L1] Luke 2:48, [L2] *patēr* and *goneis*, and [L3] Luke 1:27, 2:4 and 2:27.

**C4 (conclusion). Joseph is the biological father, and he knew Mary his wife within the espousal.**
- [L1] Genesis 4:1 gives the means of begetting: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
- [L3] Joseph and Mary were husband and wife from the espousal: "Joseph her husband" (Matthew 1:19), "Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20). The law calls a betrothed damsel "his neighbour's wife" (Deuteronomy 22:24).
- [L4] C1 requires a seed out of a Davidic man's loins. C2 makes the tribe evident by the father's house. C3 names Joseph, of David's house, as father. Genesis 4:1 gives knowing as the means. Together, this chain holds that Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal and that the child is of his loins.

## AGAINST THE DEFENDER'S LINKS

### LINK D1: "of the Holy Ghost" names covenant origin; it is not a begetter in place of a man

- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] Paul writes *ek spermatos Dauid kata sarka*, "of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3). When flesh origin is meant, *kata sarka* (according to the flesh) is written. Matthew 1:20 has *ek pneumatos hagiou* with no *kata sarka*.
- [L3] *Ek* with God or the Spirit names covenant birth in men who had fathers. John 1:13 speaks of those "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God." 1 John 5:1 says "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God."
- [L3] God claims as "my son" a son another man begat: "Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father" (1 Chronicles 28:6). The source is 2 Samuel 7:14: "I will be his father, and he shall be my son."
- [L4] The defender says "If Joseph or another man had begotten the child, the explanation would be false." The record shows otherwise. In 1 Chronicles 28:6, God's claim of sonship stands in one verse beside the father who begat. The angel's "for" (*gar*) grounds the command "take unto thee Mary thy wife." It does not deny a human father. This rests on [L1] Matthew 1:20, [L2] *ek* without *kata sarka*, and [L3] 1 Chronicles 28:6 and John 1:13.

### LINK D2: the genealogy is Joseph's line, and "as was supposed" carries no verdict

- [L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- [L2] *Egennēthē ex hēs* means "was born of her." Bearing is the mother's act, so the verb follows the mother. The verse narrates the birth, not the begetting. It does not say "not of Joseph."
- [L3] The angel addresses the line's end man as "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20). The register Matthew traces through forty-one names to reach is Joseph's.
- **On Luke 3:23.** The verb is *enomizeto* (G3543, from *nomos*, "to do by usage, be wont, suppose"). Luke uses the same form, *enomizeto*, at Acts 16:13: "where prayer was wont to be made." Prayer was actually made there, so the word of usage does not mark the thing as false.
- [L3] Luke 3:23 itself gives no female name: "the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli." The same author has Mary say "thy father" (Luke 2:48).
- [L4] The verb carries usage, not falsehood, as Acts 16:13 shows. The line Luke gives is Joseph's. So "as was supposed" cannot overrule Mary's "thy father." This rests on [L1] Luke 3:23, [L2] *nomizō*, and [L3] Acts 16:13 and Luke 2:48.

### LINK D3: the timing rows are read as written, inside the chain

- [L1] Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb." The conception is future when the angel speaks.
- [L1] Luke 1:34: "seeing I know not a man."
- [L2] *Andra ou ginōskō* is present active indicative. The defender grants this: "describes her standing." It is her state at the moment of speaking. It is not a description of the conception that 1:31 puts in the future.
- [L1] Matthew 1:24-25: "took unto him his wife: And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- [L3] Deuteronomy 20:7 separates the steps: a man "that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her."
- [L3] Matthew 1:18 dates the finding: "before they came together, she was found with child." What came together is set by 1:24, "took unto him his wife," her coming into his house.
- [L4] Matthew's order is: the finding before the taking (1:18), the taking (1:24), then no knowing until the birth (1:25). Verse 25 covers the time after the taking. It does not reach back into the espousal, when she was already "Mary thy wife" (1:20). So the record holds that Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal. This rests on [L1] Matthew 1:24-25, [L2] *ginōskō* present, and [L3] Deuteronomy 20:7 and Matthew 1:18-20.

### LINK D4: Isaiah 7:14 uses the young-woman word, and the sign is bounded in Isaiah's day

- [L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son." The 1611 margin reads "or, thou, O virgin, shalt call."
- [L2] The Hebrew is *ha-almah* (H5959, young woman). *Bethulah* (H1330) is not used. Almah stands in seven verses: Genesis 24:43; Exodus 2:8; Psalm 68:25; Proverbs 30:19; Song of Solomon 1:3; 6:8; Isaiah 7:14. Proverbs 30:19 reads "the way of a man with a maid."
- [L3] The defender's own Genesis 24:16 puts the "no man" clause on *bethulah*: "a virgin, neither had any man known her." The clause had to be added. It is not carried by *almah* at Genesis 24:43.
- [L3] Isaiah bounds the sign in his own day: "before the child shall know to refuse the evil... the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken" (Isaiah 7:16). Then: "I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son" (Isaiah 8:3), and the land is "thy land, O Immanuel" (Isaiah 8:8). Matthew 1:22-23 applies the sign. I hold that application as written. It does not add "without a man" to Isaiah's words.
- **On Hebrews 10:5.** It reads "Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me." *Katartizō* (prepare, frame) is the verb of "the worlds were framed by the word of God" (Hebrews 11:3), which is God's ordinary framing. The same epistle says "in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren" (Hebrews 2:17).
- [L4] Neither the Hebrew word nor "prepared" states conception without a man. The young-woman word, the sign bounded in Isaiah's day, and *katartizō* used of God's ordinary framing leave D4 floating. This rests on [L1] Isaiah 7:14, 16, [L2] *almah* and *katartizō*, and [L3] Genesis 24:16, Isaiah 8:3 and Hebrews 2:17.

### LINK D5 (the keystone): the defender routes the Davidic flesh through Mary, and no verse does

- [L1] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
- [L1] Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins."
- [L3] The defender's route is "Mary's descent is carried through the Davidic line that Luke 3:23 gives." But Luke 3:23 reads "the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli." No woman is named in it.
- [L3] Mary's only stated kin is priestly: "thy cousin Elisabeth" (Luke 1:36), and Elisabeth "was of the daughters of Aaron" (Luke 1:5). The Davidic house stated in the record is Joseph's (Luke 1:27; 2:4).
- **On Galatians 4:4.** "Made of a woman" is the mortality idiom: "Man [that is] born of a woman [is] of few days" (Job 14:1). It is said of John: "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist" (Matthew 11:11). John's father is named (Luke 1:13).
- [L4] The keystone needs a Davidic flesh seed without Joseph. The only route offered, through Mary, has no verse under it. The verse cited for it names Joseph and Heli. So D5 floats, and C1 to C4 stand. This rests on [L1] Romans 1:3 and Acts 2:30, and [L3] Luke 3:23, Luke 1:5 and 1:36, and Job 14:1.

## UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES (the defender's inferences lack footing in the verses cited)

1. **LINK D1.** "The text gives the origin of the begetting, and it is not human seed. That shuts out a human begetter."
   - PRESSED WITH: [L1] 1 Chronicles 28:6, "Solomon thy son... I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father."
   - [L2] *ek spermatos Dauid kata sarka* (Romans 1:3), where *kata sarka* (according to the flesh) marks flesh origin and is absent at Matthew 1:20.
   - [L3] John 1:13, "born... of God."

2. **LINK D2.** "Luke tells us the sonship was reputed, not actual."
   - PRESSED WITH: [L1] Acts 16:13, "where prayer was wont to be made."
   - [L2] *enomizeto* (G3543), the same form as Luke 3:23.
   - [L3] Luke 2:48, "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."

3. **LINK D3.** "Joseph did not know her until the birth, so he did not father the child."
   - PRESSED WITH: [L1] Matthew 1:24, "took unto him his wife."
   - [L3] Deuteronomy 20:7, "betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her."
   - [L1] Luke 1:31, "thou shalt conceive," with [L2] *ou ginōskō*, present tense.

4. **LINK D4.** "The child's body came by God's working in a virgin, and Joseph did not beget it."
   - PRESSED WITH: [L1] Isaiah 7:16, "before the child shall know to refuse the evil."
   - [L2] *almah* (H5959, young woman), with *bethulah* (H1330) absent.
   - [L3] Hebrews 2:17, "in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren."

5. **LINK D5.** "So the Davidic descent comes through the mother and does not require Joseph as the begetter."
   - PRESSED WITH: [L1] Luke 3:23, "the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli."

## PRESS TO THE DEFENDER

According to Hebrews 7:14, how is it "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda"? The law declares pedigree "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:2, 18). Name the father's house of Judah that makes it evident, from a verse quoted with its book, chapter and verse.

# ROUND 2: DEFENDER'S ANSWER

## A. Answer to the press on Hebrews 7:14

**[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood."

**Answer.** The father's house of Judah that makes it evident is the house of David, in which Joseph stands and into which he brought the child.

- **[L1]** Luke 2:4: "because he was of the house and lineage of David." **[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."
- **[L1]** Matthew 1:24-25: Joseph "took unto him his wife... and he called his name JESUS." **[L3]** Matthew 1:21: "thou shalt call his name JESUS." The angel gave Joseph the naming, and Joseph did it.
- **[L3]** Genesis 48:5 shows a house reckoning sons by taking and naming without begetting them: "Ephraim and Manasseh... are mine; as Reuben and Simeon, they shall be mine." **[L2]** *Bayith* (H1004, house, "especially family") is the unit in Numbers 1:2 and 1:18, "the house of their fathers." Numbers 1:18 reckons the house. It does not say every name in it was begotten by the man at its head.
- **[L4]** Hebrews 7:14 is evident because Jesus is registered in Joseph's house of David. Joseph took the child in and named him (Matthew 1:20, 1:24-25), and the line of the house is given in Matthew 1:1, "the son of David, the son of Abraham." Luke 2:4 gives the house, and Genesis 48:5 gives the reckoning by taking. This chain does not need Joseph to be the begetter.

## B. The Davidic route: what Mary's line adds and what Jeremiah 22:30 shuts

**[L1]** Matthew 1:11-12: "Josias begat Jechonias and his brethren... And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel." Joseph's line, which ends at Matthew 1:16, runs through Jechonias.

**[L1]** Jeremiah 22:30: "Write ye this man childless... for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah."

**[L3]** Luke 1:32, said to Mary: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."

**[L4]** The challenger's C1 and C3 require the child to be Joseph's flesh seed. Matthew 1:12 puts Joseph's begetting line through Jechonias, and Jeremiah 22:30 says no man of that seed sits on David's throne. Luke 1:32 gives the child that throne. If Joseph were the begetter, the challenger's own chain would collide with Jeremiah 22:30. If Joseph is the legal father only, and the flesh is David's through the mother (Romans 1:3), the collision does not arise. **I concede** that no verse says in words "Mary, daughter of Heli." That route is [L4], and I rest it on Luke 1:32, Luke 3:23, Romans 1:3 and Ezra 2:61, not on a naming verse.

## C. Against the challenger's chain

### Against C1 (the seed must come out of a man's loins)

**[L1]** Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."

- **[L3]** Hebrews 7:9-10: "Levi... payed tithes in Abraham. For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him." The challenger's own verse shows loins reaching an ancestor three generations back. **[L2]** *Patēr* (G3962) is defined in the sheet as "father (literally or figuratively, near or more remote)."
- **[L3]** Genesis 46:26: "All the souls that came with Jacob into Egypt, which came out of his loins." Grandsons count as "out of his loins."
- **[L4]** "Fruit of his loins" names descent from David across intervening generations. It does not name the last begetter. Mary's being of David's seed fulfils Acts 2:30 as Levi's being in Abraham's loins fulfils Hebrews 7:10. C1 therefore does not reach Joseph.

### Against C2 (tribe by the father's house)

**[L1]** Ezra 2:61: the priests "took a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and was called after their name."

- **[L4]** The challenger's own verse shows a man reckoned under his wife's father's house. So Luke 3:23, "Joseph, which was of Heli," fits a son-in-law relation (Ezra 2:61) as well as it fits a father.
- C2 also needs "evident" to mean a begotten line. Section A shows the Hebrews 7:14 evidence is the registered house.

### Against C3 (Mary's "thy father" and the narrator's "parents")

**[L1]** Luke 2:48: "behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."

**[L1]** Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" The child's next words answer Mary's "thy father" with "my Father's." **[L2]** *Patēr* (G3962, father) is the same word in both verses. In verse 49 it names God.

- **[L3]** The narrator's own naming differs from Mary's speech. Luke 2:33: "Joseph and his mother marvelled." Luke 2:43: "Joseph and his mother knew not of it." The narrator never writes "his father" and "his mother" together of these two.
- **[L2]** *Goneis* (G1118, parents) in Luke 2:27 and 2:41 is a household word for the two who reared the child. The lexicon gloss on *patēr* itself allows "figuratively, near or more remote," and John 6:42 shows the crowd saying "whose father and mother we know."
- **[L4]** Mary speaks of the child's reputed father in common speech, and the child corrects the term in the next verse. The narrator, in the same chapter, avoids "father" of Joseph. So the text itself sets a limit on the word, and C3 loses its keystone.

# Opening: Christ had no biological father

**Definition.** By "biological father" I mean the male parent whose seed, joined to the mother's, begets the child. The standard reading is that Christ had a mother, Mary, but no human male parent. His conception was the work of the Holy Ghost. Joseph was his legal and reputed father only.

## 1. Matthew's genealogy stops begetting at Joseph

[L1] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren;" The pattern is a male who begat a male.

[L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

[L2] The verb in verse 2 is ἐγέννησεν (egennēsen, G1080 gennaō), meaning "begat, fathered." In verse 16 the pattern changes. Joseph is called "the husband (ἀνήρ, anēr, G435) of Mary," not the one who begat Jesus. The relative pronoun "of whom" is ἧς (hēs), which is feminine singular. It points to Mary alone, not to Joseph or to both. The verb is ἐγεννήθη (egennēthē), "was born," which is passive.

[L3] Matthew 1:18 supports this: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

[L4] Matthew keeps "begat" for every earlier link (Matthew 1:2). In Matthew 1:16 he changes both the verb and the pronoun to the feminine singular "of whom." The grammar therefore deliberately cuts Joseph out as the begetter and names Mary alone as the one of whom Jesus was born.

## 2. The conception is attributed to the Holy Ghost, before Joseph and Mary came together

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

[L2] "Of" in both verses is ἐκ (ek, G1537), meaning "out of, from the source of." "Conceived" is γεννηθέν (gennēthen, G1080), the same root as "begat." The origin of the begetting is therefore stated as the Holy Ghost. "Before they came together" is πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν (prin ē synelthein, G4905 synerchomai), meaning "to come together," which here means to unite as husband and wife. The conception was finished before that union.

[L3] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." Joseph did not "know" (ἐγίνωσκεν, G1097 ginōskō, here used for marital knowledge) his wife until after the birth.

[L4] The text gives the source of the begetting (ἐκ, G1537, Matthew 1:20) as the Holy Ghost. It also says the couple did not unite until after the birth (Matthew 1:25). So no human male begot the child.

## 3. Mary herself, and the angel, say so

[L1] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph." [L2] παρθένος (parthenos, G3933) means "virgin, a girl who has not had relations."

[L1] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" [L2] "Know" is ginōskō (G1097), the same word as in Matthew 1:25, used of relations between a man and a woman.

[L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

[L2] "Overshadow" is ἐπισκιάσει (episkiasei, G1982), meaning "to cast a shadow over, envelop." "Therefore" is διό (dio, G1352), meaning "for which reason." The cause is stated: the Holy Ghost comes upon her and the power of the Highest overshadows her. The result is stated as "that holy thing which shall be born of thee." The source of the child is in her ("of thee") and in the divine power, and no man is named.

[L3] Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." [L2] עַלְמָה (almah, H5959) means a young woman of marriageable age. It is the word used in Genesis 24:43 for the girl who "cometh forth to draw water." Matthew applies the verse to this birth in Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son," and there the Greek is parthenos (G3933). [L4] The Isaiah sign and Matthew's use of it agree with Mary's own words in Luke 1:34. The sign was that a virgin would conceive.

## 4. Joseph is called father only as a reputed or legal father

[L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." [L2] The word is ἐνομίζετο (enomizeto, G3543 nomizō), meaning "to think, to hold by custom or opinion." Luke himself marks the relation as an opinion.

[L3] Matthew 1:20 shows Joseph called "son of David," and he is the legal link to David's house. Matthew 1:25 shows that he named the child, which is a father's legal act: "and he called his name JESUS."

**Anticipating the opponent's likely witnesses.**

[L1] John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" [L4] These are the words of unbelieving hearers, reporting what they supposed. Luke 3:23 uses the same reputed sense with "as was supposed." Also, in the same verse they object to what he says of himself: "I came down from heaven."

[L1] Luke 2:48: "behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." [L3] The answer comes in the next verse, Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" The child corrects the title. The word "father" here fits the household sense, and the child names another Father. [L2] "Father" is πατήρ (patēr, G3962), which can mean the legal or household head as well as the begetter. Which sense applies has to be decided by the context, and Luke 1:34-35 and 3:23 give that context.

## 5. Mary's flesh and the body prepared

[L1] Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law." [L2] "Made" is γενόμενον (genomenon, G1096 ginomai), meaning "to come to be." Paul names the woman as the only human parent, and he names no man.

[L3] Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me." [L2] The word is κατηρτίσω (katērtisō, G2675 katartizō), meaning "to fit out, to prepare." The body is the Father's preparation and not the product of a man's seed.

[L3] Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed." [L2] "Seed" is זֶרַע (zera, H2233). The text speaks of the woman's seed, not a man's seed.

[L3] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." [L4] This is the human descent. Combined with Luke 1:35 ("born of thee") it places the Davidic descent through Mary and not through a male begetter.

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on

1. Matthew's genealogy breaks the begetting at Joseph: it changes from "begat" (ἐγέννησεν, G1080) in Matthew 1:2 to "the husband of Mary, of whom (ἧς, feminine) was born Jesus" in Matthew 1:16, and Matthew 1:18 confirms it with "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
2. The conception is attributed to the Holy Ghost as its source: Matthew 1:20 "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost," with ἐκ (G1537, "out of"), and Matthew 1:18 "before they came together" with Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth," ginōskō (G1097).
3. Mary and the angel state the same thing: Luke 1:34 "seeing I know not a man" with ginōskō (G1097), and Luke 1:35 "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee... therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee," with dio (G1352, "for which reason") and Isaiah 7:14 "a virgin shall conceive" (H5959) as cited in Matthew 1:23.
4. Joseph's fatherhood is reputed and legal only: Luke 3:23 "as was supposed" with ἐνομίζετο (G3543), and Luke 2:48-49 where the child answers "thy father" with "my Father's business" (πατήρ, G3962).
5. Therefore Christ had no human biological father: Galatians 4:4 "made of a woman" (G1096) and Hebrews 10:5 "a body hast thou prepared me" (G2675) carry the conclusion with links 1 to 4. He was conceived of the Holy Ghost in Mary, and Joseph was his husband-of-Mary guardian and legal father.

# Opening: Christ had no biological father

**Position.** Jesus Christ had no human biological father. His conception in Mary was by the Holy Ghost, with no man's seed involved. Joseph was Mary's husband and, in law and by common opinion, the child's father. He was not the father by begetting.

---

## 1. The Gospel of Matthew states the source of the conception

**1a. [L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
**[L2]** The Greek is *ek pneumatos hagiou* (ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου, G1537/G4151/G40), "out of Holy Spirit." The preposition *ek* names the source out of which the child came. The verse also says *prin ē synelthein autous* (πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν αὐτούς), "before they came together." The pregnancy is dated before any union of Mary and Joseph.
**[L3]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." The Greek *eginōsken* (ἐγίνωσκεν, G1097) is the verb for marital knowledge. Joseph did not know her until after the birth.
**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 gives the source of the pregnancy as the Holy Ghost, and Matthew 1:25 with *ginōskō* shows no marital union before the birth. Together they leave no place for a male contributor.

**1b. [L1]** Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
**[L2]** The Greek is *to gennēthen en autē ek pneumatos estin hagiou* (τὸ ἐν αὐτῇ γεννηθὲν ἐκ πνεύματός ἐστιν ἁγίου), "that which is begotten in her is out of Holy Spirit." Here *gennaō* (G1080) is the verb of begetting. The angel names the Holy Ghost as the one out of whom the begetting is.
**[L3]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
**[L4]** Joseph, as a just man, planned to put Mary away. That shows he knew the child was not his, and the angel's correction in 1:20 supplies the explanation.

**1c. [L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
**[L2]** In the genealogy every link is *egennēsen* (ἐγέννησεν), "begat," active, with a male subject. ## D6: KEPT

D1 gives the affirmative source: "of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:18, 1:20). D2 gives the means through the woman: Luke 1:35, "born of thee." # OPENING: Christ had no biological father

**Definition.** A biological father is a man who begets a child by his own seed. I defend this: the KJV shows Christ was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost with no human male begetting. Joseph was his father only by legal reckoning and common supposition.

In Isaiah 7:14 the KJV reads "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son." **[L2]** The Hebrew *almah* (H5959) stands behind "virgin" there. Matthew 1:23 renders it *parthenos*, "virgin."

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on:

1. The conception of Christ is attributed to the Holy Ghost, not to a man: Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 ("of the Holy Ghost"), with the Greek *gennēthen* ("conceived/begotten") in Matthew 1:20, and Luke 1:35 ("The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee... therefore also"), which names the same agent as the cause.

5. Therefore Christ had no biological father: the Holy Ghost's conception (links 1 and 2), Joseph's merely supposed fatherhood (link 3), and the woman-only origin (link 4) leave no human male begetter, and Joseph is father by legal reckoning only.

# Opening Case: Christ had no human biological father

**Thesis.** The KJV presents Jesus Christ as conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, with no man as his begetter. Joseph was his legal and reputed father only.

**Definition.** By "biological father" I mean a man whose seed begot the child. I do not mean the Father in heaven. The KJV puts the conception in a different category from ordinary begetting.

---

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# Opening: Christ had no human biological father

**Thesis.** The KJV says the child Jesus was conceived in Mary, a virgin, by the Holy Ghost, and that Joseph did not beget him. Joseph was his father only as "supposed" and by legal standing. So no man was his biological father.

## 1. The genealogy breaks its own pattern at Joseph

**[L1]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob". Every link in the line ends the same way, one man begetting the next.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** The verb "begat" is *gennaō* (G1080, to beget, of a father). At the last link the text does not say "Joseph begat Jesus." It says "of whom [*ex hēs*, "out of whom," feminine singular] was born Jesus." The relative pronoun is feminine, so it points to Mary and cannot point to Joseph. Joseph is called "the husband of Mary" (*andra*, G435, husband), and the begetting formula stops there.

**[L3]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law". The Greek *genomenon ek gynaikos* means "come to be out of a woman." Only the woman is named as his human source.

**[L4]** This stands on Matthew 1:16 [L1], with the feminine *ex hēs* [L2], and on Galatians 4:4 [L3]. The writer keeps "begat" for every father in the list and withholds it from Joseph, so Jesus' human origin runs through Mary alone.

## 2. The conception is "of the Holy Ghost," before Joseph and Mary came together

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** The phrase is *ek pneumatos hagiou* (*ek*, G1537, "out of," marking source; *pneuma*, G4151, spirit; *hagios*, G40, holy). "That which is conceived" is *gennēthen*, from *gennaō*, the same verb used for each father in Matthew 1:2–16. The source of this begetting is the Holy Ghost, where the earlier links had a man.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." Joseph knew the child was not his, which is why he meant to put her away. The angel's word in Matthew 1:20 corrects him.

**[L4]** This rests on Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 [L1], with *ek* marking the source and *gennēthen* matching the genealogy's own begetting verb [L2], and on Joseph's reaction in Matthew 1:19 [L3]. The begetting is attributed to the Holy Ghost and to no man.

## 3. Mary's own words and the angel's answer exclude a human father

**[L1]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph... and the virgin's name was Mary."

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** *Parthenos* (G3933) is a virgin. *Ginōskō* (G1097, to know) is used here of relations between man and woman. The angel's reply gives the means as "the Holy Ghost shall come upon thee," and the word "therefore" (*dio*, G1352) makes the divine conception the ground of the title "Son of God."

**[L3]** Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain." "Knew" is the ordinary idiom for conjugal union leading to conception. Mary's "I know not a man" therefore denies that union.

**[L4]** This rests on Luke 1:34–35 [L1], on *parthenos* and *ginōskō* [L2], and on the idiom in Genesis 4:1 [L3]. Mary has not known a man and conceives by the Holy Ghost's coming upon her, so no man's seed is involved.

## 4. Joseph did not know her until after the birth

**[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."

**[L2]** *Ouk eginōsken* is "knew not," from *ginōskō* (to know), as in Luke 1:34. *Heōs* (G2193) means "until."

**[L3]** Matthew 1:18 says the pregnancy was found "before they came together." This confirms the order: the conception came first and the marriage union after the birth.

**[L4]** This rests on Matthew 1:25 [L1], with the idiom of *ginōskō* [L2], and on "before they came together" in Matthew 1:18 [L3]. At the time of conception Joseph had not had relations with Mary, so he could not have been the biological father.

**[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

# Opening Case: Christ Had No Human Biological Father

**Position.** By "biological father" I mean a human male who contributed to the conception. The KJV text says that Jesus Christ was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, while she was a virgin, and that Joseph was only his supposed father. [L4, resting on the layered points below]

## 1. The genealogy breaks at Joseph

**[L1]** Matthew 1:2 uses the unbroken pattern of begetting: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren". Matthew 1:16 then departs from it: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** The verb in both verses is *gennaō* (G1080), meaning "to beget" when a man is its subject and "to be born" when passive. In 1:16 the verb is passive, *egennēthē*, "was born". The relative pronoun is *ex hēs* (ἐξ ἧς), "out of whom", and it is feminine singular. Grammatically it can refer only to Mary. It cannot refer to Joseph, or to Joseph and Mary together.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:20 confirms where the weight falls: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost". The source of the conception is named as the Holy Ghost, not Joseph.

**[L4]** Matthew keeps "begat" for every man in the list. For Jesus alone he changes to a passive verb and a feminine pronoun. The text therefore withholds the father-begetting formula from the one birth it narrates in the next verses. This rests on the Greek grammar of 1:16 [L2] and the contrast with 1:2 [L1/L3].

---

## 2. The conception was "of the Holy Ghost" before Joseph and Mary came together

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** The phrase is *ek pneumatos hagiou* (ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου), "out of the Spirit, holy", which names the source. The verb *synelthein* (G4905) means "to come together". The conception is placed before that coming together.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** In Luke 1:35, *episkiazō* (G1982) means "to overshadow". *Dio kai* means "therefore also", a causal link. The title "Son of God" follows from this conception.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 gives the timing and Luke 1:35 gives the cause. Together they give a conception with a divine source and without a prior human act. Both are named in the text, and no human male is named as a contributor.

**Definition.** By "biological father" I mean a man whose seed contributed to the conception. I hold that Jesus had none. His conception was "of the Holy Ghost" in the womb of Mary, who knew no man. Joseph was his legal and supposed father, not his begetter.

## 1. Matthew states the source of the conception, and it is not Joseph

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** The phrase "of the Holy Ghost" is *ek pneumatos hagiou* (G1537 *ek*, "out of, from as source"; G4151 *pneuma*, spirit; G40 *hagios*, holy). The source of the child is named as the Spirit. "Before they came together" uses *sunerchomai* (G4905, "to come together"), which places the conception before any union with Joseph.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The angel gives the Holy Ghost as the reason Joseph need not fear. Joseph's worry would make no sense if he were the father.

**[L2]** "Conceived" here is *gennaō* (G1080), "to beget, to bring forth." It is the same verb the genealogy uses for each father in turn ("begat"). Matthew 1:20 assigns the begetting to the Holy Ghost with *ek*, "out of."

**[L4]** The genealogy repeats *gennaō* for every father (Matthew 1:2-16). The same verb in Matthew 1:20 names the Holy Ghost as the source of this child. Matthew therefore replaces a human begetter with another source, and it is not a loose statement about Joseph.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** The verb changes at the last link. Every earlier link is active, "X begat Y" (*egennēsen*, G1080). Here the verb is passive, "was born" (*egennēthē*, G1080). **[L3]** Compare Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob." The pattern of begetting runs unbroken until Joseph.

**[L4]** The pattern is X begat Y. At Joseph it becomes Joseph, husband of Mary, "of whom" (feminine) was born Jesus. The pattern, the shift of voice, and the feminine pronoun together exclude Joseph as begetter.

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** "Know" is *ginōskō* (G1097). Here it carries the sense of marital intimacy, as in Matthew 1:25. "Man" is *anēr* (G435), a male. Mary says she has not known any male.

# OPENING: Christ had no human biological father

**Position.** The standard reading holds that Christ was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, with no human male as begetter. Joseph was her husband and the child's reputed father, not his biological father. The KJV text carries this reading at each step below.

## 1. The mother was a virgin who had known no man

**[L1]** Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary."

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** *Ginōskō* (G1097), "to know," here means marital knowledge. *Anēr* (G435), "a man, a husband," stands in the same verse, Luke 1:34. Mary's present state is that she knows no man, and her question is how a conception can occur in that state.

**[L2]** The Hebrew behind the KJV's "virgin" in Isaiah 7:14 is *ʿalmāh* (H5959). The KJV renders it "virgin," and Matthew 1:23 fixes that sense with *parthenos*.

**[L4]** The footing is Luke 1:34, where Mary says she knows no man, and the *parthenos* of Luke 1:27 and Matthew 1:23. Together they show the conception was announced and received as one without a man's involvement, not as a conception whose father simply went unnamed.

## 2. The source of the conception is the Holy Ghost

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** *Ek* (G1537), "out of, from the source of," stands in both verses, in the phrase *ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of the Holy Spirit." In Matthew 1:20 *gennēthen* (G1080), "begotten, conceived," is the verb. The source of the conceiving is stated, and it is not a man.

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** *Epeleusetai* (G1904) means "shall come upon." *Episkiasei* (G1982) means "shall overshadow," that is, shall cover with a shadow. Both are verbs of divine power acting upon Mary.

**[L4]** The footing is the *ek* of Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 and the *epeleusetai* and *episkiasei* of Luke 1:35. They name the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest as the source and agent of the conception. Luke 1:35 adds "therefore also," which makes the child's title "Son of God" follow from that divine act. No human male is named as a source anywhere in these verses.

## 3. Joseph is excluded as begetter

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L3]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac." The genealogy runs on the pattern "A begat B." At the last link it breaks off, and the verb "begat" is not used of Joseph with Jesus. Joseph is called "the husband of Mary."

**[L2]** The relative "of whom" is *hēs* (G3739, feminine singular), referring back to Mary alone. Had Joseph been the begetter, the pronoun would be masculine or plural.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."

**[L4]** Joseph's response in Matthew 1:19 shows that he did not take himself to be the father. A just man who knew himself to be the father would have had nothing to put away. The angel's correction in Matthew 1:20 was needed precisely because the child was "of the Holy Ghost," not of Joseph. Footing: Matthew 1:19 with Matthew 1:20.

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."

**[L2]** *Enomizeto* (G3543), "was supposed, was reckoned by custom or law," marks Joseph's fatherhood as one of reputation and law. It is not a statement of fact about begetting.

**[L3]** On the passages sometimes pressed for Joseph as father: Luke 2:48, "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing," is Mary speaking within the supposed relationship of Luke 3:23. The child's reply in Luke 2:49 corrects it: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" Luke 1:32, "the throne of his father David," speaks of ancestry, and Romans 1:3, "made of the seed of David according to the flesh," places the line through the woman, as Galatians 4:4 does below.

**[L1]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law."

**[L2]** *Genomenon ek gynaikos* means "made out of a woman." Here *ek* again names the source, and the source is a woman only.

**[L1]** Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son."

**[L3]** Hebrews 10:5: "but a body hast thou prepared me." The body is described as prepared by God, not begotten by a man.

**[L4]** The footing is the *ek gynaikos* of Galatians 4:4 and the conceiving "in thy womb" of Luke 1:31. They give Mary a full maternal part in the conception, while Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35 name only the Holy Ghost on the other side. No row introduces a human male contributor.

---

## DECLARED CHAIN

1. Mary was a virgin who knew no man when the conception was announced. Footing: [L1] Luke 1:27 and Luke 1:34; [L2] *parthenos* (virgin) and *ginōskō* (to know); [L3] Matthew 1:23 with Isaiah 7:14.
2. The source of the conception was the Holy Ghost, not a man. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:18, Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35; [L2] *ek* (out of, from the source of), *epeleusetai* (come upon) and *episkiasei* (overshadow).

4. The child's human nature came from Mary alone, by divine preparation. Footing: [L1] Galatians 4:4 and Luke 1:31; [L2] *ek gynaikos* (out of a woman); [L3] Hebrews 10:5.
5. Christ had no human biological father: he was conceived of the Holy Ghost in the virgin Mary, and Joseph was his father in law and reputation only.

# OPENING: Jesus had no biological father

**Term.** By "biological father" I mean a man whose seed joined with the mother's to cause the conception. I hold that the KJV states a different cause for the conception of Jesus, and that this leaves no place for such a father.

## 1. Matthew 1:16 changes the verb and the pronoun at Joseph

[L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

[L2] The verb "begat" is ἐγέννησεν (egennēsen, G1080 gennaō, to beget, father). It is used for every father in the list. For Jesus the verb becomes ἐγεννήθη (egennēthē, was born, the passive of the same root). The relative pronoun "of whom" is ἧς (hēs), which is feminine singular. It can only point back to Mary, not to Joseph. Joseph is called ἄνδρα (andra, husband, G435), not the one who begat.

[L3] Matthew 1:20 supports this: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

[L4] The list uses "begat" for every father and then does not use it of Joseph toward Jesus. The feminine pronoun names Mary alone as the one "of whom" he was born. Verse 20 supplies the reason for the change. Two layers carry the inference: the verb and pronoun in verse 16, and the stated source in verse 20.

## 2. The conception is stated to be of the Holy Ghost

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

[L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

[L2] In Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 "of" translates ἐκ (ek, out of, from, marking source and origin). The phrase is ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου (ek pneumatos hagiou, out of the Holy Spirit). In Luke 1:35, ἐπελεύσεται (epeleusetai, shall come upon, G1904) and ἐπισκιάσει (episkiasei, shall overshadow, G1982) name the agent. The word "therefore" is διό (dio, for which reason). The holy thing is called "the Son of God" because of this conception.

[L4] The angel gives the cause of the conception, and it is the Holy Ghost, not a man. Luke 1:35 ties the title to that cause with "therefore." Footing: the ek of source in Matthew 1:20 and the causal dio in Luke 1:35.

## 3. Mary and Joseph had not come together, and he did not know her

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together."

[L2] συνελθεῖν (synelthein, G4905 synerchomai, to come together, here as husband and wife).

[L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."

[L2] ἐγίνωσκεν (eginōsken, G1097 ginōskō, to know). It is used here of marital union.

[L3] Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain." The Hebrew יָדַע (yada, H3045, to know) is used of union that results in conception.

[L1] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

[L4] Matthew's wording places the conception before any union and keeps Joseph from union until after the birth. Mary's question in Luke 1:34 uses the same verb of knowing, and the angel's answer in verse 35 names the Holy Ghost. Footing: ginōskō/yada as a sexual term in Matthew 1:25 and Genesis 4:1, and the question and answer of Luke 1:34-35.

## 4. The sign, the seed of the woman, and the prepared body

# Opening: Christ had no biological father

**Position.** [L4] On the KJV record, Jesus had a biological mother, Mary, and no biological human father. His conception was "of the Holy Ghost" in a virgin who had not known a man. Joseph was his legal and household father, "as was supposed," but not his begetter.

---

## 1. The text states the source of the conception

**[L1] Matthew 1:18:** "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L2]** "Of" translates *ek* (out of, from as source). "Came together" is *synelthein* (to come together, here as husband and wife). The conception is dated before any union and assigned to the Spirit as its source.
- **[L3] Matthew 1:20:** "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." Here *to gennēthen* (that which has been begotten) is followed again by *ek* (out of). The same verb *gennaō* (to beget, to bring forth) is used elsewhere of fathers, so the text puts the Spirit where a father's begetting would stand.
- **[L4]** From Matthew 1:18 (union comes after the conception) and from *ek* in Matthew 1:20 (the Spirit as source), the begetting is assigned to the Holy Ghost. No place is left for a human begetter.

## 2. Mary's question and the answer given

**[L1] Luke 1:34:** "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- **[L2]** *ginōskō* (to know, here of marital knowledge) is in the present tense. Mary is a virgin ([L1] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph") and has no relation with a man.
- **[L1] Luke 1:35:** "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- **[L2]** *dio kai* (for which reason also, "therefore also") makes the Spirit's coming the ground of the title. *Episkiazō* (to overshadow) describes divine power, not a man's act.
- **[L4]** The question asks how a conception can occur without a man. The answer names the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest and does not name a man. That answers the question as asked, so the conception is without a human father.

## 3. Matthew 1:16 breaks the begetting pattern

**[L1] Matthew 1:2:** "Abraham begat Isaac." The genealogy runs on with the active *egennēsen* (begat) down the male line.
**[L1] Matthew 1:16:** "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- **[L2]** The verb changes to the passive *egennēthē* (was born). The relative pronoun *hēs* (of whom) is feminine singular. It refers to Mary alone, not to "Joseph."
- **[L4]** From the active "begat" of verse 2 to the passive "was born" with a feminine "of whom" in verse 16, the text stops saying "Joseph begat Jesus" at the one place where the pattern would require it. Joseph is called "the husband of Mary," and Mary alone is named as the one of whom Jesus was born.

## 4. Joseph's reaction fits the record

**[L1] Matthew 1:19:** "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
**[L1] Matthew 1:20:** "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."

- **[L1] Matthew 1:25:** "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." **[L2]** *Eginōsken* (was knowing, imperfect tense) denies continued marital knowledge until after the birth.
- **[L4]** Matthew 1:19 (Joseph supposes the child is not his) and Matthew 1:25 (no union until after the birth) together fix the order: no relation before the birth, conception by the Spirit.

## 5. The sign and the body

**[L1] Isaiah 7:14:** "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."
- **[L2]** The word behind the KJV's "virgin" is *almāh* (H5959). **[L3] Genesis 24:43:** "when the virgin cometh forth to draw water" uses the same word for Rebekah, who was described in Genesis 24:16 as one "neither had any man known her."

- **[L3] Hebrews 10:5:** "a body hast thou prepared me." **[L2]** *katērtisō* (thou hast fitted, prepared) assigns the body's preparation to God.
- **[L4]** Isaiah 7:14 as applied in Matthew 1:23 gives a virgin conceiving. Hebrews 10:5 gives God as the preparer of the body. Both agree with a conception that had no human father.

## 6. The curse on Jeconiah's seed

**[L1] Jeremiah 22:30:** "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David."
**[L1] Matthew 1:12:** "Jechonias begat Salathiel." Joseph's line runs through this man.
- **[L2]** *Zera'* (seed, H2233, offspring) is the word in Jeremiah 22:30.

- **[L4]** If Jesus were Joseph's seed, he would be Jechonias's seed (Matthew 1:12), and Jeremiah 22:30 would bar the throne Luke 1:32 gives him. If Jesus is "of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3) through Mary, whose descent is the one the text gives alongside Luke 1:27's "house of David" for Joseph, the legal line comes through Joseph and the flesh through the mother. This is consistent with no biological father.

## 7. How the texts that name a father are answered

# Challenger, Round 1: Christ had a biological father, Joseph, the named son of David

**Position.** The promise sets the Christ's flesh "out of" David's body and loins. The record names one man in that line as the child's father: Joseph, "of the house of David." "Of the Holy Ghost" and "the Son of God" are the covenant words the record also gives to men who have fathers. My chain follows, then my presses on D1 through D6.

---

## CHALLENGER'S DECLARED CHAIN

**C1. The promised seed comes out of a man's body.**
- **[L1] 2 Samuel 7:12:** "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom."
- **[L2]** "seed" is zera' (H2233, "seed, posterity"). "bowels" is me'eh ("inward parts, body").
- **[L3] Psalm 132:11:** "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne." (margin: "body: Heb. belly")
- **[L3] Acts 2:30:** "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne." **[L2]** osphys (G3751, "loins," the seat of procreative power).
- **[L3] Romans 1:3:** "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh." **[L2]** spermatos (G4690, "seed"), with kata sarka ("according to the flesh").
- **[L4]** David's bowels, his body and his loins are named as the source, and the seed is named "according to the flesh." So the Christ's flesh is set out of a man's body in David's line. This rests on [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12 and [L2] zera'/osphys/sperma, with [L3] Acts 2:30 and Romans 1:3.

**C2. The seed of David reaches the child through the named father, Joseph.**
- **[L1] Matthew 1:20:** "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." (margin: "conceived: Gr. begotten")
- **[L1] Luke 1:27:** "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David."
- **[L3] Luke 2:4:** "because he was of the house and lineage of David."
- **[L3] Numbers 1:18:** "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers." **[L2]** bayith (H1004, "house, family") and 'ab (H1, "father").
- **[L3] Hebrews 7:14:** "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."
- **[L3]** The record names Joseph as father in four voices:
  - Mary: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" (Luke 2:48).
  - The narrator: "the parents brought in the child Jesus" (Luke 2:27).
  - A disciple: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph" (John 1:45).
  - The angel: "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20).
- **[L4]** Pedigree is declared "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:18, bayith + 'ab). The man of "the house of David" in these rows is Joseph (Luke 1:27; 2:4). So the descent that makes it "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda" (Hebrews 7:14) runs through Joseph.

**C3. "Of the Holy Ghost" and "Son of God" are covenant origin and empowerment, given beside a father.**
- **[L1] Luke 1:32:** "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David." The title and the throne are given in verse 32. Mary asks "How shall this be" at Luke 1:34, after that.
- **[L3] 2 Samuel 7:14:** "I will be his father, and he shall be my son."
- **[L3] 1 Chronicles 28:6:** "Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father." One verse calls Solomon David's son and God's son.
- **[L3] Psalm 2:7:** "Thou [art] my Son; this day have I begotten thee." (margin: "the decree: or, for a decree") The New Testament applies it three times:
  - to the resurrection: "in that he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee" (Acts 13:33);
  - to the priesthood (Hebrews 5:5);
  - beside 2 Samuel 7:14: "I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son" (Hebrews 1:5).
- **[L3] Romans 1:4:** "declared [to be] the Son of God with power ... by the resurrection from the dead." (margin: "declared: Gr. determined")
- **[L2]** At Matthew 1:20, ek ("out of") with gennaō ("beget") and the Spirit follows the same pattern as **[L3] 1 John 5:1:** "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God: and every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him." (margin: "Gr. has been born") The same holds at **[L3] John 1:13**, "born ... of God." These are believers, and each has a father among men.
- **[L4]** The record gives "my son" to Solomon while it calls him "thy son" to David (1 Chronicles 28:6). It applies "begotten" (Psalm 2:7) to the resurrection (Acts 13:33). It says ek + gennaō of God of men with fathers (1 John 5:1). So these words name covenant origin, and they stand beside a father in the flesh.

**C4. The union is within the espousal.**
- **[L1] Genesis 4:1:** "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived." (margin: "Cain: that is, Gotten, or, Acquired") This is the record's stated means of begetting.
- **[L1] Matthew 1:19:** "Joseph her husband." **Matthew 1:20:** "Mary thy wife." **[L3] Deuteronomy 22:24:** the betrothed damsel is "his neighbour's wife."
- **[L2] Luke 1:34:** andra ou ginōskō ("I know not a man") is present indicative. It states her state when the angel spoke.
- **[L3] Luke 1:31:** "thou shalt conceive in thy womb" is future (syllēmpsē, "thou shalt conceive").
- **[L1] Matthew 1:24–25:** "took unto him his wife: And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." **[L2]** heōs hou ("till") bounds the span. It runs from the taking to the birth.
- **[L3] Deuteronomy 20:7:** "what man is there that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her?" The law names the taking as a step after betrothal. Matthew 1:18's "before they came together" stands beside Matthew 1:24's "took unto him his wife."
- **[L4]** The canon begets by knowing (Genesis 4:1). Joseph and Mary are husband and wife from the espousal (Matthew 1:19–20; Deuteronomy 22:24). The abstinence of Matthew 1:25 is bounded to the span after the taking. So Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal.

**C5 (keystone). Christ had a biological father, Joseph.** [L4] This rests on C1 (seed out of a man's loins), C2 (Joseph the named son of David), C3 (covenant words given beside a father) and C4 (the union within the espousal).

---

## PRESSES ON THE DEFENDER'S CHAIN

**Against LINK D1.**
- **[L1] Luke 1:31:** "thou shalt conceive in thy womb." **[L2]** syllēmpsē is future ("shalt conceive").
- **[L3] Luke 1:34:** ou ginōskō is present ("I know not").
- **[L4]** Her present state and a future conception stand in sequence. Matthew 1:25's "till" (heōs hou) opens at "took unto him his wife" (Matthew 1:24). By Deuteronomy 20:7, the taking follows the betrothal. So D1's "through the birth" fits the span from the taking to the birth. The conception falls in the espousal before it.

**Against LINK D2.**
- **[L1] Matthew 1:20** names "Joseph, thou son of David" and "Mary thy wife" in the same sentence that says "of the Holy Ghost."
- **[L2]** ek + gennaō of God is said of believers: "born of God ... begotten of him" (1 John 5:1). The same is said at "born ... of God" (John 1:13).
- **[L3]** The verbs of Luke 1:35 are anointing and presence verbs:
  - eperchomai (G1904, "come upon") is said of the apostles: "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you" (Acts 1:8; margin: "or, the power of the Holy Ghost coming upon you").
  - episkiazō (G1982, "overshadow") is said of the cloud: "there came a cloud, and overshadowed them" (Luke 9:34). It is also said of Peter's shadow, "might overshadow some of them" (Acts 5:15; margin: "or, in every street").
- **[L4]** On D2's dio kai: the dio kai ("therefore") in Luke 1:35 connects back to Luke 1:32, not forward to biological divine paternity. The title and "the throne of his father David" are given in Luke 1:32, before Mary asks "How shall this be" in Luke 1:34.
- On D2's [L3] Matthew 1:2: gennaō of fathers there fits C2. The line runs through fathers, down to "Joseph, thou son of David."

**Against LINK D3.**
- **[L1] Luke 2:48:** "thy father and I." **[L3] Luke 2:27:** "the parents." These are Mary's own words and the narrator's own word.
- **[L2]** enomizeto (G3543, "was supposed, was wont") is the same form as Acts 16:13, "where prayer was wont to be made."
- **[L3]** On Luke 2:49, "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?": the next verses give "he went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject unto them" (Luke 2:51). Two fathers stand in one scene, as two stand in one verse at 1 Chronicles 28:6.
- **[L3]** On hēs (feminine, "of whom"): Eve says "another seed" of Seth, and "Adam knew his wife again" (Genesis 4:25; margin: "Seth: Heb. Sheth: that is Appointed, or, Put"). The mother is named, and the father is named.

**Against LINK D4.**
- **[L1] Isaiah 7:14:** "a virgin shall conceive." (margin: "or, thou, O virgin, shalt call") **[L2]** 'almah (H5959). The KJV gives the same word as "the maid" (Exodus 2:8) and "the way of a man with a maid" (Proverbs 30:19).
- D4's own "neither had any man known her" stands at Genesis 24:16 with bethulah (H1330, "virgin"). That is a different word from Genesis 24:43's 'almah.
- **[L3]** The sign is bounded and fulfilled in Isaiah's day:
  - "before the child shall know to refuse the evil ... the land ... shall be forsaken of both her kings" (Isaiah 7:16);
  - "I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son" (Isaiah 8:3; margin: "went: Heb. approached");
  - "O Immanuel" (Isaiah 8:8).
- **[L3] Jeremiah 31:22:** "How long wilt thou go about, O thou backsliding daughter? ... A woman shall compass a man." In that verse the woman is the backsliding daughter, and "a man" stands in the verse.
- I hold Matthew 1:23 whole: "a virgin shall be with child" (margin: "or, his name shall be called"). Luke 1:27 says "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph." The virgin of the fulfilment is an espoused wife.

**Against LINK D5.**
- **[L1] Galatians 4:4:** "made of a woman, made under the law." The same "of a woman" is said of John:
  - **[L3] Matthew 11:11:** "Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist."
  - **[L3] Luke 1:13:** "Fear not, Zacharias ... thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son."
- "Sent" is said of John too: "There was a man sent from God, whose name was John" (John 1:6).
- **[L3]** The prepared body "likewise took part of the same" (Hebrews 2:14). It was "in all things ... made like unto [his] brethren" (Hebrews 2:17). And "he took on [him] the seed of Abraham" (Hebrews 2:16; margin: "Gr. taketh not hold of angels, but of the seed of Abraham he taketh hold").
- **[L4]** Each of D5's words, "sent" and "made of a woman," is said of a man whose father is named. So they fit a body prepared out of David's loins (Acts 2:30).

**Against LINK D6 (keystone).** D6 rests on D1 through D5, each pressed above. Its own words, "the human nature came from Mary alone," are charged below.

---

## UNSUPPORTED-L4 PREMISES

1. **LINK D1:** "So no man, Joseph included, had known her when the child was conceived."
   ASSUMES: the conception fell inside the span Matthew 1:25 covers.
   ROWS GIVE: "took unto him his wife" (Matthew 1:24); "thou shalt conceive in thy womb" (Luke 1:31).
   PRESSED WITH: Luke 1:31, Matthew 1:24, Deuteronomy 20:7.

2. **LINK D2:** "The text names no human male source, so there is no room for a biological father among men."
   ASSUMES: "of the Holy Ghost" names the begetter of the flesh.
   ROWS GIVE: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:20); "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God" (1 John 5:1).
   PRESSED WITH: 1 John 5:1, Acts 1:8, Luke 9:34, Luke 1:32.

3. **LINK D3:** "Joseph's reaction to the pregnancy (Matthew 1:19) and the angel's correction of it (Matthew 1:20) show he knew he was not the source."
   ASSUMES: Joseph knew himself to be outside the begetting.
   ROWS GIVE: "Joseph her husband, being a just [man] ... was minded to put her away privily" (Matthew 1:19); "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" (Luke 2:48).
   PRESSED WITH: Luke 2:48, Luke 2:27, 1 Chronicles 28:6.

4. **LINK D4:** "A sign (Isaiah 7:11) fulfilled in a virgin (Isaiah 7:14, Matthew 1:23) is a conception without a man's part."
   ASSUMES: the sign sets aside a man's part.
   ROWS GIVE: "I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son" (Isaiah 8:3, margin "Heb. approached"); "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph" (Luke 1:27).
   PRESSED WITH: Isaiah 7:16, Isaiah 8:3, Proverbs 30:19.

5. **LINK D5:** "The human body came from Mary through God's preparing."
   ASSUMES: the prepared body came by a route apart from David's loins.
   ROWS GIVE: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ" (Acts 2:30); "he also himself likewise took part of the same" (Hebrews 2:14).
   PRESSED WITH: Acts 2:30, Hebrews 2:14, Hebrews 2:17, Matthew 11:11.

6. **LINK D6:** "the human nature came from Mary alone."
   ASSUMES: Mary's flesh carries the seed of David.
   ROWS GIVE: "a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David" (Luke 1:27); "thy cousin Elisabeth" (Luke 1:36); "his wife [was] of the daughters of Aaron, and her name [was] Elisabeth" (Luke 1:5).
   PRESSED WITH: Romans 1:3, Luke 1:27, Luke 1:36, Luke 1:5.

---

## QUESTION TO THE DEFENDER

**[L1] Hebrews 7:14:** "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda." **[L3] Numbers 1:2 and 1:18:** pedigrees are declared "by the house of their fathers."

According to Hebrews 7:14, how is it evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda, given the law of Numbers 1:2 and 1:18? Answer from the house of the fathers your rows name.
